turmeric.season: May - June (Kharif pre-monsoon) or August - September

climate.sunlight: Thrives in warm, humid tropical conditions; tolerates 30-50% shade with higher curcumin synthesis

soil.drainage: Must be well-drained. Water stagnation for > 24 hours triggers severe rhizome rot.

stages.description: Deep ploughing 2 to 3 times to a depth of 25-30 cm. Incorporate 25 tonnes/ha of well-decomposed FYM (Farm Yard Manure) or compost. Prepare raised beds of 1.2m width, 15-20cm height, and convenient length with 40cm drainage channels between beds.

Select healthy, disease-free mother or primary finger rhizomes weighing 35-45g each with at least 2 viable buds. Treat rhizomes by dipping for 30 minutes in a solution of Trichoderma harzianum (10g/L) or Carbendazim (2g/L) to prevent seed-borne rhizome rot.

Plant rhizomes at a spacing of 30cm between rows and 20-25cm within rows at a depth of 4-5cm. Cover with loose topsoil and immediately apply a thick organic mulch using green tree leaves (12-15 tonnes/ha) to conserve moisture and suppress early weeds.

First irrigation immediately after planting. During early emergence, irrigate at 7-10 day intervals. During active vegetative growth and rhizome bulking (days 75-180), maintain soil moisture above 60% of field capacity with drip irrigation (2.5-4.0 mm/day). Withhold irrigation 15-20 days before final harvest.

Recommended fertilizer dose: 60:50:120 kg N:P2O5:K2O per hectare. Apply entire P2O5 and 1/3rd K2O as basal application at planting. Top-dress N and remaining K in 2 equal split doses at 45 and 90 days after planting, accompanied by earthing up.

Major disease: Rhizome Rot (Pythium / Fusarium) - manage by improving drainage and drenching with Copper Oxychloride (3g/L) or Trichoderma. Major pest: Shoot Borer (Conogethes punctiferalis) - spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) or Neem Oil (5ml/L) at first sign of central shoot yellowing.
Sprouting: 15-30 days after planting. Vegetative tillering: 45-90 days. Rapid rhizome bulking: 90-180 days. Senescence: 190-250 days where leaves begin to turn yellow and dry downwards.

Maturity reached when 80-90% of pseudostems and foliage turn completely dry and lodge on the ground (approx. 8-9 months after planting). Cut dry tops close to ground level. Dig beds carefully with a spade or tractor-mounted digger without bruising or cutting rhizomes.

Separate mother rhizomes from finger rhizomes. Wash thoroughly with clean water. Boil fingers in water or steam-boil until white froth appears and a blunt probe penetrates easily (45-60 mins). Sun-dry boiled fingers on clean tarpaulins for 10-15 days until moisture drops below 10% (metallic ring when dropped).
Store dried fingers in food-grade gunny bags with polythene lining in cool, dry, rodent-proof godowns. For seed rhizomes, store in sand-layered pits under deep tree shade with good ventilation.

coconut.season: Planting: May - June (South-West Monsoon) or Sept - Oct

climate.sunlight: Full sun required for palm crown (> 2000 hours bright sunshine/year)

soil.drainage: Deep well-drained soil with water table at least 1.5 - 2.0 m below surface.

stages.description: Dig pits of 1m x 1m x 1m size at 7.5m x 7.5m or 8m x 8m spacing. Fill bottom 30cm with red earth and 20kg FYM mixed with 1kg bone meal and 100g chlorpyrifos dust to repel white ants.
Select 9-12 month old vigorously growing seedlings having 6-8 leaves with broad leaf blades and early leaf splitting, and collar girth of at least 10-12 cm.
Plant seedling in the center of the pit such that the nut is covered with soil while the collar is left exposed. Firm the soil well around the base.
Adult palm requires 45 to 60 litres of water per day via drip system. Install 4 emitters per palm placed 1.0 - 1.5m away from the trunk. During peak summer, increase to 80-100 L/palm/day.
Per adult palm per year: 500g N (1.1kg Urea), 320g P2O5 (2kg Rock Phosphate), and 1200g K2O (2kg MOP) applied in 2 split doses in May-June and Sept-Oct, plus 50kg FYM and 1kg agricultural lime.
Major pests: Rhinoceros Beetle (apply neem cake + sand 1:1 in top leaf axils) and Red Palm Weevil (install pheromone traps). Disease: Bud Rot - spray 1% Bordeaux mixture on the crown before monsoon.
Clean the palm crown twice a year (before monsoon and post-monsoon), removing dried leaves, spathes, and insect debris.
Harvest mature 11-12 month old nuts at 30 to 45 day intervals. Tender coconuts for drinking are harvested at 7 months.
Store harvested mature nuts under shade for 2-3 weeks for seasoning (reduces moisture in husk and increases kernel firmness before dehulling).
Dehusked nuts can be sold fresh or converted to copra in sun drying yards or copra dryers to reach 6% moisture content.

banana.season: Year-round in South India; main planting Feb-April and Aug-Oct

climate.sunlight: High light requirement; partial shade tolerated in multi-tier agroforestry

preferred_types: Red Sandy Loam with organic matter
soil.drainage: Requires deep well-drained fertile soil with minimum 1m topsoil depth.

stages.description: Plough field 3-4 times. Dig pits of 45cm x 45cm x 45cm at 1.8m x 1.8m spacing (or 2.5m x 2.5m when intercropped in coconut alleys). Add 10kg FYM and 250g neem cake per pit.
Use healthy, virus-free sword suckers weighing 1.5 - 2.0 kg or secondary hardened tissue culture plants with 5-6 broad leaves.
Trim sucker roots and peel pseudo-bark. Dip in solution of Carbendazim (2g/L) + Chlorpyrifos (2.5ml/L) for 20 minutes before planting.
Banana needs 15-20 litres/plant/day in winter, increasing to 25-35 L/day during summer bunch emergence. Drip fertigation provides optimal yield.
200g N, 60g P2O5, 300g K2O per plant per cycle applied across 4 split applications at 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th months.
Remove side suckers systematically until flowering to direct all energy into main mother plant stem.
Earth up soil around pseudostem at 3rd month to prevent waterlogging and give support. Provide bamboo or wooden propping once bunch emerges.
Remove the male floral bud (navel) after all female hands have opened. Cover bunches with perforated blue polypropylene sleeves.
Harvest when bunch angles round off and fruit changes from dark green to pale green (75-80% maturity for export, 90% for local market).
De-hand bunches carefully, wash in alum water to remove latex, air dry, and pack in CFB boxes. Ethylene gas ripening at 16-18°C.

black-pepper.season: Planting with onset of South-West Monsoon (June - July)

climate.sunlight: Requires 50-70% filtered sunlight; perfectly suited for climbing coconut and arecanut standards

preferred_types: Clay Loam with high organic humus
soil.drainage: Must have rapid drainage; root zone susceptible to water stagnation.

stages.description: Trailed on existing mature coconut or arecanut trees. Dig planting pits of 50cm x 50cm x 50cm on the north-eastern side of standard tree, 30cm away from trunk.
Select rooted runner cuttings from high-yielding varieties (Panniyur-1, Panniyur-2, Karimunda) raised in polythene bags with at least 5-6 healthy nodes.
Plant 2 rooted cuttings per coconut tree or 1 per arecanut tree. Fill pit with topsoil and 5kg compost. Tie vine gently to tree bark with coir yarn.
Requires light, frequent irrigation during summer dry months. A single dripper delivering 8-10 L/vine every alternate day prevents leaf shed.
Apply 100g N, 40g P2O5, and 140g K2O per vine per year in 2 splits (May-June and August-September) along with 10kg cattle manure.
Tie vines to standard every 30cm as it grows. Limit vine height to 6-8 meters on coconut trunks to facilitate hand harvesting.
Drench basin with 0.2% Copper Oxychloride or apply Trichoderma harzianum (50g mixed with 5kg neem cake) at onset of monsoon.
Harvest spikes when 1 or 2 berries on the spike turn bright orange or red. Pick whole spikes by hand using tall ladders.

Separate berries from stalks by hand or mechanical thresher. Dip berries in boiling water for 1 minute (blanching) to accelerate black skin color development. Sun-dry on clean floor for 7-10 days to 10% moisture.
Grade into bold and regular berries. Store in clean double-gunny or polypropylene bags lined with polythene in a dry, ventilated storehouse.

black-pepper.data_source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Spices Research (IISR) Calicut Pepper Production Bulletin

groundnut.season: Kharif: June - July; Rabi/Summer: November - January

climate.sunlight: High sunlight requirement; suitable as intercrop in young orchards (< 7 yrs)

soil.drainage: Light friable soil essential to allow easy peg penetration and pod expansion.

stages.description: Plough to a fine tilth to 15-20 cm depth. Soil must be loose and friable. Apply 10 tonnes/ha FYM and 200 kg gypsum per ha as basal.
Treat kernels with Rhizobium culture (250g/10kg seed) + Trichoderma viride (4g/kg seed) to fix atmospheric nitrogen and prevent collar rot.
Sow at 30cm between rows and 10cm between plants at 4-5cm depth. Seed rate: 100-120 kg kernels/ha.
Critical stages for irrigation: Flowering (20-30 DAS), Pegging (35-50 DAS), and Pod development (55-80 DAS). Avoid water stress during pegging.
Apply 200 kg/ha gypsum at 40-45 DAS around plant base followed by light earthing up to supply calcium for pod filling and reduce empty shells (pops).
Keep weed-free until 45 DAS. Do NOT disturb soil or hoe once pegging begins, as mechanical disturbance breaks emerging pegs.
Tikka leaf spot: spray Mancozeb (2g/L). Spodoptera caterpillar: spray NPV (Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus) or neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%).
Maturity indicated by yellowing and shedding of lower leaves, inner pod shell showing dark brown/black veins, and seed coat displaying pink color.
Pull plants when soil is slightly moist. Invert vines under the sun for 2-3 days, then strip pods mechanically or manually.
Sun-dry pods to 7-8% moisture content before storage. Store in gunny bags stacked on wooden pallets in dry godowns to prevent aflatoxin development.
